Maya R.: Quick check — ran compact-summarizer v1 on the support multi-turn slice with aggressive compression. Latency looks great but quality shifted. Metrics below.
Jin K.: Which slice + prompts? paste numbers pls.
Maya R.: slice=support-chat-1k (avg 420 tokens). fp16 Rouge-L 28.4 -> compact-int4 Rouge-L 25.1. p95 latency fp16=480ms int4=330ms. GPU tks/sec +1.9x. cost/1k tokens fp16=$0.045 int4=$0.028. Hallucination rate up ~2.1%.
Orion P.: Oof. Is the regression concentrated on long-thread summaries or particular intent types? any priming sensitivity?
Maya R.: Mostly long-thread (>8 turns). Tried removing priming variations, toggled prefix caching, warmed KV cache both runs. Pattern persists. Hallucinations skew to omitted context bits rather than invented facts.
Sam G.: From product POV — for legal/account-closure flows we need <1% hallucination. That 2.1% is concerning.
Maya R.: Agreed. My rough econ calc: if we move 20% traffic to int4 we save ~38% on model cost for that fraction -> ~$9k/mo. But estimated increase in escalations from quality drop costs ~$4.5k/mo. Net ~+$4.5k/mo. Need to weigh risk.
Jin K.: Can you share the exact numbers and a proposed routing strategy?
Maya R.: Econ summary: fp16 cost/1k $0.045, int4 $0.028. Site baseline tokens/month ~200M. With 20% shift net savings ~= $4.5k/mo after estimated escalation costs. Routing suggestion incoming.
Maya R.: Routing config suggestion (proto):
```yaml
route: support-summarize
if: intent in [legal, account_closure]
  model: compact-sum-fp16
else:
  model: compact-sum-int4
fallback: compact-sum-fp16 if rouge_drop > 2.5
```
Orion P.: Can we add a lightweight on-the-fly safety classifier to steer problematic queries to fp16? cheap and effective if tuned.
Sam G.: Also propose 1% holdback fp16 for drift detection + daily eval. A/B plan: 50/50 on non-sensitive traffic for first 48h then widen.
eval-bot: Auto-eval ran 200 random holdback examples -> int4 mean Rouge-L drop = 3.0 (sd 0.9). Hallucination flagged in 4/200 samples (manual confirm suggested).
Maya R.: Plan: 2-week canary with route + 1% fp16 holdback + automated eval daily. Rollback triggers: persistent rouge_drop > 2.0 for 48h OR hallucination rate >1.2% over 12h.
Jin K.: I'll wire a feature flag and the dashboard panels (p95 latency, rouge-l trend, hallucination rate, cost delta).
Maya R.: I'll draft a short GTN README with sample eval queries, cost calc sheet, and the holdback playbook. Link to draft: https://go/redwood/sum-int4-econ
Orion P.: Nice work. If the classifier reduces false negatives we can widen int4 to 40% safely.
Sam G.: Thanks — please add an explicit checklist for compliance team signoff before expanding to legal intents.
Maya R.: Will do.
Orion P.: :rocket: Good plan.
file_notes: canary + routing + econ snapshot for compact-summarizer int4 bring-up
